item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence on program design and macro outcomes, but little direct 2024 evidence showing actual subgroup-by-subgroup distribution of benefits by region, class, or gender. There is no clean 2024 dataset here showing whether specific regions systematically captured more gains, or whether opposition supporters were excluded from benefits in a measurable way. So the best-supported conclusion is mixed: Tinubu had multiple inclusive policy designs, but actual 2024 outcomes remained highly unequal and the record contains real patronage/favoritism and regressive-cost signals.","evidence":[{"title":"World Bank Approves New Financing for Nigeria to Improve Health Outcomes, Safety of Dams, and Irrigation Services","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-09-26","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services","summary":"The package targeted health, basic education governance, and irrigation/hydropower resilience, explicitly aiming at service delivery bottlenecks that affect poorer households and lagging areas. This is strong evidence for broader public-goods distribution.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Supporting Nigeria’s Homegrown Reforms: New World Bank Financing for Inclusive Growth and Revenue Diversification","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-06-13","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/13/supporting-nigeria-homegrown-reforms-new-world-bank-financing-for-inclusive-growth-and-revenue-diversification","summary":"The Bank said the reform package was meant to raise non-oil revenue, safeguard oil revenue, create fiscal space for public services, and scale up support to vulnerable households. That is negative evidence for fairness across groups because the state responded coercively to largely lower-income protest grievances.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.4","5B.5","5B.7"]}]}
